exposure: distance travelled by mother to hospital
cohort: The study included 1180 neonates born to mothers using emergency medical services (EMS) at term gestation (37-42 weeks) in five Indian states.
finding: Neonates born to mothers who travelled <=60 km and reached a health facility <=120 min had 67% lower odds of early neonatal death compared to those with longer travel distance or time.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was identified as a significant variable on univariate analysis and was adjusted for in the multivariable logistic regression model.
